content.text:
`whoami` and `list_workspaces` now include celld-backed workspaces. The full suite is green with the new tests included.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm test` | 66 files, 734 tests passed (8 new) |
| `pnpm check:types` | clean |
| `pnpm check:cycles` | no cycles |
| `pnpm check:lint` | 0 warnings |

**Root cause.** The filesystem hub cannot reference celld, so `whoami` in `src/hub/identity.ts` and `list_workspaces` in `src/hub/workspace.ts` only scan filesystem storage. Both operations carry no `workspaceId`, so the routed handler in `src/celld/routed-handler.ts` treated them as plain passthrough and never consulted the route registry. `workspace_status` worked because it names a workspace and gets routed to the cell.

**What changed.**
- New `src/celld/cell-listing.ts` exports `listActiveCells`, which snapshots every active route and reports unreachable cells separately. It is the single source for "which celld workspaces exist" so the MCP operations and the HTTP read model cannot drift apart.
- The routed handler now intercepts the two global reads. It calls the inner handler first, so agent resolution and its errors are unchanged, then merges celld data. `whoami` appends each active workspace whose cell state lists the agent as a member. `list_workspaces` appends each active workspace with the same summary shape as filesystem entries plus a backend marker, and marks unreachable cells the same way the HTTP listing does.
- With no active routes, both operations return the inner result object by identity, preserving byte-for-byte filesystem behavior.
- The read model was refactored to use the shared helper. Its output is unchanged, and the existing HTTP tests still pass.

**One judgment call.** An unreachable cell cannot prove membership either way, so `whoami` omits it rather than guessing, while `list_workspaces` still shows the row flagged as unreachable. That mirrors the read model's existing handling.

The new test file is `src/celld/__tests__/routed-handler-global-reads.test.ts`. It covers celld-only members, mixed backends with ordering, provisioning and uninitialized and unreachable cells, inner-error propagation, and the untouched-result guarantee. No existing test file or dependency was modified.

**Root cause.** The filesystem hub cannot reference celld, so `whoami` in `src/hub/identity.ts` and `list_workspaces` in `src/hub/workspace.ts` only scan filesystem storage. Both operations carry no `workspaceId`, so the routed handler in `src/celld/routed-handler.ts` treated them as plain passthrough and never consulted the route registry. `workspace_status` worked because it names a workspace and gets routed to the cell.

**What changed.**
- New `src/celld/cell-listing.ts` exports `listActiveCells`, which snapshots every active route and reports unreachable cells separately. It is the single source for "which celld workspaces exist" so the MCP operations and the HTTP read model cannot drift apart.
- The routed handler now intercepts the two global reads. It calls the inner handler first, so agent resolution and its errors are unchanged, then merges celld data. `whoami` appends each active workspace whose cell state lists the agent as a member. `list_workspaces` appends each active workspace with the same summary shape as filesystem entries plus a backend marker, and marks unreachable cells the same way the HTTP listing does.
- With no active routes, both operations return the inner result object by identity, preserving byte-for-byte filesystem behavior.
- The read model was refactored to use the shared helper. Its output is unchanged, and the existing HTTP tests still pass.

**One judgment call.** An unreachable cell cannot prove membership either way, so `whoami` omits it rather than guessing, while `list_workspaces` still shows the row flagged as unreachable. That mirrors the read model's existing handling.

The new test file is `src/celld/__tests__/routed-handler-global-reads.test.ts`. It covers celld-only members, mixed backends with ordering, provisioning and uninitialized and unreachable cells, inner-error propagation, and the untouched-result guarantee. No existing test file or dependency was modified.
